overall: Atlanta is starting June 21st under a complete overcast sky with a very low ceiling of just 91 meters and near-saturated air (dewpoint 69.8°F vs. current temp 71.6°F), conditions that are actively suppressing morning warming. The day is trending cooler than the NWS 88°F forecast would imply at this early stage, though peak heating is still several hours away.

max_temp_prediction: The most likely outcome is a daily high in the 86–87°F range, driven by cloud clearing during the late morning and early afternoon as the NWS forecast implies ('mostly sunny'), with peak heating arriving around 16–17h ET per model consensus. The main downside risk is that the dense low overcast (ceiling ~300 ft) and saturated boundary layer delay clearing and cap the afternoon peak closer to 84–85°F; upside to 88–89°F is possible but requires rapid cloud erosion, which current humidity argues against. Confidence is moderate — the META model is strongly convicted on 86–87°F but intraday uncertainty remains elevated given how overcast and stalled conditions are at 08:00.
